newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes slip in modest Wednesday trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes slip in modest Wednesday trading.

text.p: Weekly inventory stock data showing builds in crude and products inventories deflated U.S. cash crude prices Wednesday.

Domestic grade differentials also showed signs of weakness, attracting weaker bids for both sour and sweet barrels. July Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) remained stagnant at a premium of 15 cents to the NYMEX futures screen.
Benchmark July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged at $20.35 a barrel, roughly even with late Tuesday prices. NYMEX trade headed to the close around 10-15 cents weaker at $20.15-25 a barrel.

U.S. Department of Energy inventory data released Wednesday afternoon showed builds for crude and products stocks, seconding the American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers released late Tuesday. Builds, however, were not as dramatic as seen in the APIs.

For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James ranged around a 16 cents discount to July WTI/Cushing. West Texas Sour/Midland was sold a few cents weaker at $1.60 under benchmark, and July Postings Cushing Plus sold steady at $1.93 to $1.95.
